verdict.rationale: Sentry documents a first-party self-hosted distribution that runs "all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything," and a long-term user reports running it rock-solid for years. Sentry itself limits it to a "minimal setup" for "simple use cases" with "no guarantees or dedicated support," and users report self-hosted releases lag SaaS and resource needs grow until a 32GB server runs only Sentry. missing for 10: supported or guaranteed self-hosting beyond simple use cases, timely parity with SaaS releases, documented manageable resource footprint at scale.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: How you can run all of Sentry on your own server, without paying anything.
Sentry offers and maintains a minimal setup that works out-of-the-box for simple use cases. This version comes with no guarantees or dedicated support.
They have run self-hosted Sentry at work for a couple of years and it has worked fantastically; once running it is rock-solid.
